'Has this been the case in Auckland?' people are right to ask. 

I think the critical difference is that the Supercity was essentially a merger of metropolitan councils. 

Otago would be one metro council, swallowed by (in some cases quite wealthy) rural and provincial districts

We'll be left to pay to fix the insane rates of development in Queenstown Lakes, while they refuse to spend any money whatsoever on the wellbeing of coastal communities.

Which makes this the only example we need to know that an Otago wide unitary authority could be the death knell for Dunedin.

Even if we could get all five Dunedin ward reps to support the long term future of our our city (highly unlikely given the current circumstances) they'd still be voted down by the clean coal lot inland. 

This is true of climate action, adaptation, transport planning, and so on.

Stopping cities from spending money on the things that they need and want - but which aren't valued by conservative politicians - has been the dream of our right wing governments since Rodney Hide's failed Supercity plan in Auckland, and reform of the Local Government Act.

The Mayor is right. The ORC high jacking this process at the 11th hour, with the vocal support of the DCC far right, has been a masterclass in predatory delay. 

But the comms on this has all been fronted by staff, when (given it's political nature) it probably should have been led by elected reps.

Option 1 is to continue with two separate plan changes, Option 2 (recommended) is to do one for the entire precinct.
